nodes.label: Hermes
nodes.summary: Brais's production fork of NousResearch/hermes-agent, run as the COO/control plane for BigLobster and its customers: one multiplexed gateway, a profile per customer, cron-driven content agents, a PR auditor and an incident watcher.
details: Fork of NousResearch/hermes-agent (MIT); UPSTREAM_VERSION v0.22.5 (recorded 2026-10-23, upstream renumbered from v2026.9.24); repo br41s/hermes-sandbox
A customer or project is a Hermes profile (native profiles; no custom namespacing layer)

One container: Coolify app on a Netcup VPS in Nuremberg (project hermes-eu), moved off Zeabur 2026-11-05 (EU residency for GDPR; clears a Spanish Plesk geo-block); earlier Zeabur Frankfurt from 2026-07-22, Jakarta before
Panel at hermes.biglobster.top (Nous OAuth); webhooks at hook.biglobster.top; Telegram forum supergroup with one topic per profile; CEO-only access
Control plane for the other projects: changes here can affect FinView, biglobster, grow-shop and every repo Hermes touches
Two invariants: per-conversation prompt caching is sacred; core is a narrow waist (capability goes in plugins/skills)
Deploy as rarely as possible (owner's rule 2026-10-01): every deploy restarts the gateway

nodes.label: hermes-sandbox repo
nodes.summary: The fork's GitHub repo: upstream code plus fork-only dirs (fork_ext, auditor, incidents, remediation, merge_on_green, agent prompts, ops, docker).
details: br41s/hermes-sandbox; the repo is public (2026-09-18 decision: Actions minutes are free); BIGLOBSTER_SETUP.md still says private

Fork-only code: hermes_cli/fork_ext, cron/fork_ext, auditor/, incidents/, remediation/, merge_on_green/, gap-hunter/, onsite-seo/, infographic/, shorts/, offsite-geo/, content-updater/, maintenance/, ops/, scripts/provision_bl_client.py
AGENTS.md is upstream's dev guide (read per section); CLAUDE.md is fork-specific and inert to the Hermes runtime
Fork workflows: ghcr-publish.yml, shorts-studio.yml, infographic-check.yml, osv-scanner.yml, upstream-drift.yml (most others are upstream's)
Dependency alerts triaged to zero crit/high on 2026-09-18 (242 -> 22); osv-scanner.toml is a decision log

Branch protection on main (Brais, 2026-11-05): requires only the `All required checks pass` gate job, not strict; admins can bypass; no force-push or deletion. Auto-merge had merged #513 before its tests finished

nodes.label: NousResearch/hermes-agent
nodes.summary: Upstream open-source agent framework (MIT) that hermes-sandbox forks.
details: Fork merges upstream release tags only, one reviewed PR per week; currently on v2026.9.24
Workspace rule: check it before building any agent, tool or skill from scratch

nodes.label: Image build (GitHub Actions)
nodes.summary: ghcr-publish.yml builds the Hermes image on every push to main and publishes it to GHCR as :latest and :sha-<commit>.
details: Image ghcr.io/br41s/hermes-sandbox, ~2.7 GB (Playwright + Chromium + Python + Node), s6-overlay as PID 1
Tag contract: git rev-parse --short=9 on both the workflow and deploy.sh (a shallow clone gives 7 and breaks the pull)
Concurrency group cancels superseded builds, so intermediate merge commits are never deployable
Since 2026-09-18 (PR #271/#280). Older docs (BIGLOBSTER_SETUP.md, ops/deploy-zeabur.md) describe Cloud Build as primary and say Actions is not enabled; newer decision log wins
Cloud Build (cloudbuild.yaml) remains as the deploy.sh --build fallback
The auto-memory note 'GitHub Actions never run' (2026-09-10) is stale for this repo; deploy-automation-plan.md records the correction

Auto-deploy from CI was rejected 2026-09-22: it would put a hosting credential in CI and let the auditor's auto-merge ship to prod unattended (still true on Coolify: deploy.sh runs from the owner's Mac)
2026-11-05 (#513/#514): ops/deploy-zeabur.md and the Zeabur isolate runbook now carry a header marking them historical; zbpack.json removed; deploy docs describe Coolify

nodes.label: deploy.sh
nodes.summary: scripts/deploy.sh stops the Hermes app in Coolify, moves its image tag to sha-<commit>, starts it, verifies the container runs that commit, and refuses unsafe deploys.
details: Run by the owner after pulling main; --status, --dry-run, --verify-file, --yes, --build, --force-in-flight
Refuses a non-main branch, an unpublished image, and (under --yes) a deploy while any cron run is claimed/running in any store

Never Coolify's Redeploy: it can start the new container before stopping the old one, and two gateways would poll Telegram with one bot token and write the same volume and state.db. The script refuses to move the tag if the old container has not gone; a failed ssh never reads as a stopped container (auditor review, #513)
'Pod is serving' is not 'Telegram is listening': wait for 'Cold boot: dropping Telegram updates' then 'Gateway running'
Gateway stop grace is S6_KILL_GRACETIME 20s; SIGKILL leads to a PRAGMA quick_check on the 2.2 GB state.db at next boot (up to ~4 min)

Since 2026-11-05 (#513) it reaches Coolify's API over SSH (the API listens only on the server's localhost), with the token read on the owner's Mac and sent on stdin; `zeabur service update tag` is gone
Rollback = the same by hand in Coolify with the previous sha-<commit>; :latest is never used; verify with a file only the new image has or /opt/hermes/.hermes_build_sha

nodes.label: Hermes service (Zeabur)
nodes.summary: The former Hermes container: Zeabur prebuilt-image service `hermes` in project hermes-eu on the Frankfurt dedicated server. Replaced by the Coolify app (coolify-hermes) on 2026-11-05.
details: Retired 2026-11-05: Hermes moved to Coolify on the Netcup VPS (hosting slice node coolify-hermes); the Zeabur service was kept suspended as rollback until the account closes
Facts that still hold on Coolify (env only in the app env, pod commands as the hermes user, Coolify R2 Postgres dumps, Traefik files) are on the Hermes platform node and in deploy.sh / backup nodes
Zeabur era: env vars lived only in Zeabur env; no liveness probes, so rollouts every 1-2h were benign; 2026-07-22 migration used root SSH rsync of /opt/data

nodes.label: Gateway (multiplex)
nodes.summary: The single gateway process (s6 slot gateway-default) that serves Telegram and the cron ticker for every profile.
details: gateway.multiplex_profiles is on (upstream default; the fork's opt-out was removed in stage 3 step 4); rollback is a code revert and redeploy
boot_reconcile writes one gateway.profile_routes entry per bound Telegram topic; a bound topic with no route is dropped, never answered by the default profile
Never bring up a gateway-<profile> slot for a secondary profile (double-serves it) and never copy TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN into a profile
HERMES_FORK_SCOPE_PROCESS_ENV=1 lets the launch profile's secret scope fall back to the service env; health probe: hermes_cli.fork_ext.process_env_scope --check must say VERDICT: OK
First multiplex rollout 2026-09-28 silenced Telegram; re-enabled after the process-env scope fix

Logs: /opt/data/logs/agent.log (infrastructure only; use Langfuse for what an agent did), profiles/

/logs/agent.log for moved jobs

2026-10-17: the Buzz platform adapter splits long messages by UTF-8 bytes (60,000 under the relay's 65,536 limit) instead of cron output being cut at 4000 with an unreadable 'saved to' footer (PR #470)

2026-10-23 bug (fixed): after upstream v0.22.5 a served secondary kept a credential-free local adapter, so the "is the adapter map empty?" test took it for its own bot; every biglobster and auditor delivery failed `platform telegram not configured` until the fix. A satellite borrows the primary's bot only while it holds no messaging adapter other than `local` (gateway/profile_routing.py)
TELEGRAM_* allowlists and bot token live in the Coolify app env

nodes.label: Cron scheduler
nodes.summary: The cron ticker inside the gateway: one store per profile (plus the default store), per-profile serial pools, agent and no-agent script jobs.
details:
Default store /opt/data/cron/jobs.json; every named profile has its own profiles/

/cron/jobs.json (all fork `profile` jobs moved into profile stores, cohorts 2026-10-02..04)
cron.max_parallel_jobs: 1 per named profile; main (default) store unbounded; profiles run side by side
agent.max_turns 90; HERMES_CRON_MAX_RUNTIME 1800s wall clock; provider request_timeout_seconds 600 (auditor 420)
A store's cron expressions run in that profile's own config.yaml timezone (unset = UTC); bl-shoroban set to Asia/Bangkok
Each job holds a frozen copy of its prompt; repo .prompt files reach it only via `hermes cron sync-prompt` (deploy first)
Panel 'Run now' only queues the job; the ticker starts it within 60s

`hermes cron move --to-profile

` moves a job between stores keeping id, phase and history; afterwards use `hermes -p

cron ...`

nodes.label: Boot reconciler (cont-init)
nodes.summary: s6 cont-init hooks run on every container boot; 03-biglobster-config calls boot_reconcile to sync env, pin config, seed profiles and clone repos.
details: Hooks: 01-hermes-setup, 015-supervise-perms, 02-reconcile-profiles, 03-biglobster-config
Syncs Coolify app env into main and per-profile .env (INJECT list); TENANT_EXCLUDE keeps OPENROUTER/EXA/HF/PEXELS/Langfuse keys out of rented tenants

Pins config: web backend exa, image_gen provider openrouter (skipped for profiles with their own FAL_KEY), video_gen provider huggingface, agent.max_turns 90, cron.max_parallel_jobs 1, request_timeout_seconds
Seeds per-profile SOUL/repos.txt/routing.env from docker/profiles and generates gateway.profile_routes per bound topic
Clones/pulls profile repos and isolated BigLobster checkouts (biglobster-seo, -gaphunter, -infographic, -translation) with timeouts so a git stall cannot hang boot
Pins the auditor's dedicated GitHub identity and token; registers the gsc MCP server on the biglobster profile only

nodes.label: Agent git commit guard
nodes.summary: Client-side git hooks installed into every agent clone that block mass-deletion commits and direct agent pushes to main.
details: Pre-commit blocks commits deleting more than 10 tracked files (override HERMES_ALLOW_MASS_DELETION=1); chains each repo's own .githooks/pre-commit
`git commit --no-verify` is hard-blocked; pre-push layer blocks agent identities pushing directly to main
Origin: 2026-06-22 blind git add -A deleted 48 cover images and 404'd the blog for ~22h
Installed through core.hooksPath in cont-init section 6c; blocked commits append to blocked-commits.jsonl, surfaced by the incident watcher

nodes.label: bl_site_* tools (client-site write path)
nodes.summary: bl_site_publish / bl_site_product / bl_site_health / bl_site_redirect: the single audited HTTP path rented agents use to write to a client's bl-site-package site.
details: Authenticated with that profile's own panel password (X-Automation-Key header where Turnstile blocks a bare login); never a database, never a repo
Facts are the site's, prose is the agent's: identifiers, change fingerprints and publish eligibility are decided server-side

Blog posts go live immediately (status hardcoded to published) but every PUT snapshots the replaced body (bl-site-package >= 1.8.0, restorable from Blog -> Historial); agents pass author and base_hash
Product sheets save as drafts unless publication is explicit; redirects stay pending unless the match tier is gtin/mpn (gate reads the tier back from the site)
Toolsets are declared per job (restrictive allowlist) so a prompt and its real capabilities cannot drift silently

2026-11-02 (#507): create_blog_post refuses a new post that states percentages with no source link off the client's own site (links in HTML comments or without a host do not count); prices and catalogue counts are exempt

nodes.label: Rental provisioner
nodes.summary: scripts/provision_bl_client.py creates a rented bl-site-package client as a Hermes profile with its own key, config and daily agent jobs; triggered by the CEO via Telegram or by a Stripe-confirmed webhook from BigLobster.
details: Creates profile bl-<client>, writes .env (client's own OpenRouter key, optional FAL_KEY/Pexels key, site URL, panel password), config.yaml (model default deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash, web.search_backend ddgs), SOUL and the cron jobs

AGENT_SOURCES: gap-hunter, seo, onboarding-content (one-shot), product-articles, product-sheets, infographic, maintenance, site-setup (one-shot), content-updater, shorts; schedules hashed into a 02:00-06:00 window; deliver is always `local`
Webhook: POST /api/bl/rental/provision with HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp + raw body, 300 s replay window, secret BL_RENTAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET; refuses all requests if the secret is unset
Removal is manual: remove each job, then `hermes profile delete <slug>`
BYOK: rented profiles bill their own OpenRouter key; the boot reconciler never overwrites it with ours
--runs-per-week (1-7, default 2, #510) spreads each agent's off-peak slot over that many days from a hashed weekday; Website Maintenance stays daily because its run is the availability check
2026-11-05: AGENT_RENTAL_SETUP says rental hosting is decided per customer, no default host (#515)

nodes.label: Model routing
nodes.summary: How Hermes picks models: everything goes through OpenRouter with explicit provider pins, per-role defaults, no-training/no-storage routing, and BYOK for tenants.
details: Main default deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash (CEO 2026-09-20); fallback z-ai/glm-5.3-flash since 2026-10-09 (was tencent/hy3); vision deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash; set by env vars HERMES_DEFAULT_MODEL / HERMES_FALLBACK_MODEL, reconciled each boot

Auditor profile exempt: orchestrator deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731; system and content reviewers/judge moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (2026-10-10, replacing xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash which returned stubs on 6 of 9 judge calls; minimax-m3 and deepseek-v4.1-flash passed as fallbacks); separate HERMES_AUDITOR_OPENROUTER_API_KEY keeps spend off the shared cap. GLM is a valid fallback but not a judge (mandatory reasoning)

Keys rotated 2026-10-09 to the LLC's OpenRouter account (hermes, hermes-auditor); boot_reconcile rewrites INJECT keys into every non-tenant profile at each boot, so rotation is Zeabur env + full restart
Job pins: all 6 pinned jobs use deepseek-v4.1-flash, no hy3 pins remain (2026-10-09)

provider_routing.data_collection=deny forced on main and every profile by boot_reconcile, passed to the cron agent, sent on every auditor judge request and by the WhatsApp assistant (#425, 2026-10-10); replaced the account-wide ZDR switch. Gaps: auxiliary vision/summaries and image/video plugins send no provider block. meta/muse-image has no zero-retention provider
Images: openrouter bytedance-seed/seedream-4.5 (~$0.04 per art plate) for BigLobster; tenants with their own FAL_KEY use fal (flux-2 klein, or seedream via fal)
Web research: Exa for BigLobster profiles; rented tenants use the free ddgs backend. video_gen provider pinned to huggingface at boot
Always name the dated OpenRouter slug and pass --provider openrouter on interactive switches (vendor segment like tencent/ or openai/ would auto-detect a direct provider with no key)

nodes.label: Langfuse tracing (BigLobster project)
nodes.summary: Langfuse project holding traces for the default profile and BigLobster-owned profiles; the source of truth for what an agent actually did.
details: Plugin plugins/observability/langfuse; keys HERMES_LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY/SECRET_KEY, base URL unprefixed HERMES_LANGFUSE_BASE_URL/LANGFUSE_BASE_URL
Query /api/public/v2/observations with fields=core,basic,io (never /traces; v1 endpoints removed 2026-11-16); a 401 can still return {"data": []}, always print the HTTP status
Session id is cron_<job_id>_<YYYYMMDD>_<HHMMSS>; a killed run has no root span but its finished tool calls are findable by sessionId
Known gap: GENERATION observations carry no usage/cost, so LLM cost per run is not observable

nodes.label: Langfuse tracing (rentals project)
nodes.summary: A separate Langfuse project, with its own key pair, that all rented-client profiles trace into.
details: Keys HERMES_RENTAL_LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY/_SECRET_KEY set in the service env 2026-09-29 (Zeabur then, Coolify app env now); pinned into rental .env on every boot (rental_langfuse_pin)
If unset, both key names are pinned empty (never stripped), which disables tracing instead of failing open onto BigLobster's keys
Rationale: a client agent can read its own .env, and a key pair reads every trace in its project
A rental run is only findable with the rental keys; BigLobster's project returns an honest empty result

nodes.label: Auditor (PR reviewer)

`python -m auditor.pending` lists unreviewed PRs (cap 10/run, ~90 tool-call budget); each PR is tiered system or content (fail-safe: unknown paths = system)

Repo set = engine + union of docker/profiles/*/repos.txt: hermes-sandbox, biglobster, FinView, grow-shop-api, grow-shop-landing, SocialAgenda, bl-site-package
Orchestrator deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 via OpenRouter; reviewers kimi-k2.6 since 2026-10-10; own OpenRouter key; request deadline 420s

Attaches gated remediation proposals; known gap: does not cover failures of no-agent script jobs such as the nightly backup; reads the host volume backup's outcome in Drive (not its host log, so a failed final rclone check after the dumps landed shows only there)
Dedicated tokens: HERMES_DEP_ALERT_GITHUB_TOKEN; no-agent cron scripts never see GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN

ChatMemo backup heartbeat: reads a secret gist the Mac backup rewrites after each verified dump; briefs after 50h of silence or an unreadable heartbeat; blind (401/403/404, file gone) is its own incident; outside the deployment it is a no-op with no network call
